policy.decision: escalate if ANY rule fires; auto_handle only when all rules pass
policy.safety_asymmetry: a false auto-handle is far costlier than a false escalation — the policy is deliberately conservative

rules.name: private_state_domain
rules.fires_when: predicted intent ∈ {account_icloud, billing_purchases, repair_warranty, security_privacy, support_process}
rules.why: the correct next step depends on private state the system cannot see (order, quote, account, identity, official channels); public generic advice risks harm
rules.provenance: Phase 2 taxonomy typically_escalated hints (4 of 5) + documented Phase 6 account_icloud refinement (decision log D25)

rules.name: unmatched_intent
rules.why: no groundable issue class; an evidence draft would rest on irrelevant historical cases

rules.name: sensitive_content
rules.why: payment/order language or private data (email, phone, card-like number) in the message must not be answered — or echoed — by a public auto-reply
rules.provenance: Phase 5 safety rule 4, applied at the decision layer as defense-in-depth against intent misclassification

rules.name: intent_confidence_gate
rules.why: Phase 3 measured 0.780 mean confidence on correct vs 0.508 on wrong test predictions; below the threshold the routing itself is unreliable
rules.provenance: INTENT_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD fixed since Phase 3 (.env, single source of truth)

rules.name: retrieval_evidence_gate
rules.why: Phase 4 measured Recall@5 0.826 above vs 0.586 below the threshold; weak evidence produces clarifying questions, which a human should own
rules.provenance: RETRIEVAL_THRESHOLD fixed since Phase 4 (.env, single source of truth)

criteria: ESCALATE (money/account stakes): the issue involves purchases, refunds, payments, order delivery, warranty/repair pricing, or Apple ID/iCloud account access — wrong public advice could cause financial or account harm, or resolution needs private details.
ESCALATE (safety/off-topic): the message is abusive, violent, off-topic, or does not describe a technical issue — there is no groundable problem, and a casual auto-reply is a brand risk.
ESCALATE (ambiguity): the message is too vague or mixes many topics to safely answer with ONE public reply.

ESCALATE (unusable device / data at stake): the device is bricked/unusable or real-world data (tickets, work access) is at risk — wrong troubleshooting steps could destroy data; needs priority human help.

AUTO_OK: a single, clear technical software/hardware issue with standard troubleshooting evidence available — a grounded draft (with DM-redirect where the evidence style demands it) is safe to publish.
ground_truth.annotator: assignment author (single pass, before running the policy on this set)

ablation_vs_phase5_gates.description: the Phase 5 preview auto-handled a message iff both numeric gates passed (intent_pass AND retrieval_pass); this ablation isolates what the Phase 6 domain/content rules add

honest_caveats: n=29 (the golden test split): every rate carries the wide exact CI reported alongside it — 0 false-autos in 10 should-escalate messages bounds the true false-auto rate below ~26% at 95% confidence, not at zero.
Ground truth is ONE human's judgement against fixed written criteria; no inter-annotator agreement exists.
The policy's numeric gates reuse the Phase 3/4 thresholds fixed before Phase 6; the domain rules reuse the Phase 2 taxonomy hints. No rule was tuned on these test labels.

The runtime signals (predicted intent, confidence, top-1 score) come from the recorded Phase 5 run; re-running generation would produce slightly different confidences/scores and could shift borderline decisions.
Precision/recall treat 'escalate' as the positive class; the operationally dominant error (over-escalation) is reported separately because it costs human minutes, not customer safety.
